01.2

AutoDS → CJdropshipping Product Research & Sourcing System

Last edited in OneNote Monday, September 21, 2026

Find a product. Validate demand. Source the exact product. Confirm profitability.

This workflow uses AutoDS to discover potentially profitable pet products and CJdropshipping to find and fulfill the exact same product at a competitive cost.

Our Target: $20 net profit per sale

The distinction is that AutoDS helps you discover a product worth investigating, while CJdropshipping becomes your intended supplier once you have verified the exact product, its delivered cost, and availability.

Your $20 profit target should be calculated after product costs, shipping, payment fees, advertising, and an allowance for refunds—not simply the difference between the retail price and the supplier's listed price.

NOTE: Reference 01.1: Product Opportunity Report (Research) here as a recommentation for the products to select in AUTO DS.

Step 1 — Find products using AutoDS

Log in to AutoDS and open Marketplace.

AutoDS currently documents discovery features including Hand-Picked Products, Trending Products, product analysis, supplier listings, shipping filters, and profit-related filters.

NOTE: AutoDS's Hand-Picked Products section includes a profit-range filter, but its displayed potential profit is not a verified net profit for your Shopify store. Its pricing system also uses estimated costs and fees when projecting profit.

Research from AUTODS Products as suggested on the results of research from 01.1 Section .

Record the information for each shortlisted product

Before moving to CJdropshipping, create a product research record containing the product title, AutoDS listing URL, original supplier URL if available, supplier price, estimated US shipping cost, suggested selling price, performance indicators, and product specifications.

Download the product images for comparison. Save any model number, dimensions, material details, color variants, and original manufacturer information shown in the listing.

Important: Do not import the product into your live Shopify catalog yet. Your first goal is to establish whether it is worth researching and whether CJ can supply the exact version.

Step 2 — Establish the $20 profit requirement

A product with a $20 markup does not necessarily produce $20 in profit.

For this workflow, I recommend treating $20 as your target contribution per sale after product cost, shipping, payment fees, estimated advertising acquisition cost, and a refund/replacement allowance.

In Claude – Model: Opus, use this prompt to building an interactive dropshipping profit calculator:

Attach this file on the CHAT (Interactive Calculator.txt)
📎 Interactive Calculator.txt attached text file
Download .txt
You are an expert full-stack web developer, e-commerce financial analyst, and user experience designer.

Create a fully functional interactive application called "CCAC Pet Essentials — Dropshipping Profit Calculator" for a Shopify business using AutoDS for product discovery and CJdropshipping for sourcing.

Build a REAL WORKING Claude Artifact, not a mockup. If possible also provide a downloadable standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript version. Use a responsive professional dashboard with white background, subtle gray sections, rounded inputs, green positive results, red losses, amber warnings, USD formatting, two-column desktop and single-column mobile layout. All results must recalculate immediately whenever an input changes.

INPUTS AND DEFAULTS:
Desired profit per sale T = $20, with working preset buttons $10, $15, $20, $25, $30 and arbitrary custom positive values.
Retail selling price P = $59.99.
Product cost C = $8.
Supplier shipping S = $4.
Meta advertising cost per sale A = $15.
Refund/replacement allowance R = $1.
Payment fee F = 2.9%.
Fixed payment fee X = $0.30.
Other variable costs O = $0.

All inputs must accept decimals and zero, reject negative and invalid inputs, and validate F as 0 <= F < 100. Assume a one-unit order, entered retail price as total revenue, and no assumed customer shipping charge or sales tax.

CALCULATIONS:
Payment fee = P*F/100 + X.
Total variable expenses = C+S+A+R+O+payment fee.
Estimated profit = P-total variable expenses; preserve negative results.
Maximum affordable supplier product cost = P-S-A-R-O-payment fee-T.
Maximum advertising cost per sale = P-C-S-R-O-payment fee-T.
Minimum retail selling price = (T+C+S+A+R+O+X)/(1-F/100), rounded UP to the nearest cent.
Profit margin = estimated profit/P*100, or N/A if P=0.
Perform calculations at full precision and format results afterward.

RESULTS DASHBOARD:
Show estimated profit prominently, target met/below target status, maximum supplier product cost, maximum advertising cost per sale, minimum retail selling price, profit margin, total variable expenses, and payment fees. For negative maximum allowable costs, explain that the target is not achievable even with zero cost in that category.

COST BREAKDOWN:
Show retail price, product cost, shipping, advertising, refund allowance, payment fees, other costs, total expenses, and profit. Add a responsive visual breakdown that honestly displays costs exceeding revenue.

AUTODS TO CJ SOURCING:
Add optional product name, AutoDS URL, CJ URL, and product notes fields. Show the maximum affordable CJ product purchase price and compare it with actual CJ product cost. Display supplier cost within budget or supplier cost exceeding budget without claiming that a product is guaranteed viable.

A WORKING "COPY CALCULATION RESULTS" BUTTON:
Copy product information, all inputs, costs, calculated outputs, and target status. Confirm success only after copy works and provide a manual-copy fallback if clipboard access fails.

A WORKING "RESET TO DEFAULT VALUES" BUTTON:
Restore every numerical default and clear optional product details, with immediate recalculation.

BUSINESS NOTES:
Explain that the result is estimated contribution after the entered variable costs but before fixed overhead and taxes; advertising CAC must be updated from actual Meta Ads purchases; supplier shipping must reflect the real destination; payment fee defaults are illustrative; this calculator does not guarantee demand or profitability.

IMPLEMENTATION:
Use React for the Artifact if appropriate. For the optional standalone version use self-contained HTML, CSS, and vanilla JS with no paid dependencies, backend, database, signup, or API keys. Do not create inert buttons or dummy charts. The entire app must work in desktop and mobile browsers.

VERIFY WITH THESE DEFAULTS:
P=59.99, T=20, C=8, S=4, A=15, R=1, F=2.9, X=0.30, O=0.
Expected payment fee $2.04; expenses $30.04; profit $29.95; maximum product cost $17.95; maximum advertising cost $24.95; minimum retail price $49.75; margin 49.9%.
Use full precision internally. Also test positive, below-target, negative-profit, zero-price, $50 target, over-budget supplier cost, invalid inputs, copy, and reset.

FINAL DELIVERABLE:
Create and display the fully working interactive Claude Artifact now, and provide a downloadable standalone HTML file if supported. Do not return only a plan, explanation, pseudocode, or incomplete code.
On the Chat itself, type this: "Hi Claude, please create the calculator as an Artifact so I can interact with it directly".
Claude will create your calculator as a widget if code execution is NOT turned on. It's fine, you can use the widget instead.

Below is an example of a product that you would select:

For example, if your selling price is $49.99, your product costs $8, shipping costs $4, advertising costs $15, payment fees are $3, and your refund allowance is $1, the remaining contribution is $18.99.

That product does not meet your $20 target under those assumptions.

At the same selling price and other expenses, your maximum CJ product cost would be $6.99.

Use the maximum affordable product cost as a sourcing constraint when searching CJdropshipping. If a supplier cannot meet it, consider a different retail price, a bundle, or a different product rather than assuming advertising costs will be lower.

Step 3 — Find the Exact Product in CJ Dropshipping

Once you have identified a candidate on AutoDS, open CJdropshipping .

CJ supports searching for products by image, and you can submit a sourcing request if its existing catalog does not contain the product you need.

Method A: Find the product using image search
Open your selected product's AutoDS listing and save its clearest product image.
Go to CJdropshipping and locate the search bar at the top of the website.
Select the camera/image search option and upload the saved product image.
Examine the returned products and open any visually matching listing.
Compare the design, materials, dimensions, package contents, operating mechanism, and variants against the original AutoDS listing.
Save the CJ product URL and supplier price for the matching candidate.

CJ's image-search feature is designed to locate matching catalog products, but visual similarity alone does not establish that two listings are for the same model or manufacturer.

Method B: Search by product name and specifications

If image search does not return a confident match, search using the descriptive product name, model number, or manufacturer identifier.

For example, for a dog nail scratch board with a treat drawer, you could try the following searches:

When searching, look for matching design features rather than relying solely on the product title. Generic titles are frequently used across similar products.

Step 4— Verify that the AutoDS and CJ Products are identical

This is an important checkpoint before purchasing a sample, importing the product, or creating advertising videos.

Exact-product verification checklist

Compare the original AutoDS product against the proposed CJ supplier listing.

Same manufacturer or model number, where identifiable
Same physical design and shape
Same dimensions and material
Same operating mechanism and functions
Same included accessories and package quantity
Same colors, sizes, and selected variants
Same product specifications and electrical requirements, if applicable
Supplier confirms the product is an exact match
Actual sample matches the product used in photographs and advertising

Step 5— Import the confirmed CJ product into Shopify

Once CJ has confirmed the product, you have received and checked a sample, and your financial assumptions support further testing, you can prepare the Shopify listing.

Connect your CCAC Pet Essentials Shopify store to CJdropshipping using CJ's supported store authorization process.
Locate the verified CJ product and use its listing or store-connection functionality to prepare the Shopify product.
Check all variants, product photographs, quantities, shipping settings, retail prices, and inventory information.
Confirm the Shopify product and variant mappings correspond to the correct CJ product and variants.
Place a test order and confirm that it reaches the intended CJ fulfillment workflow.
Verify the actual delivered product and its quality before launching paid advertising.

01.4

New Product Branding Recommendations from Claude

Last edited in OneNote Friday, September 25, 2026

Use this prompt every time you want Claude to evaluate whether multiple CJ products should be combined into one branded Shopify offer.

This prompt is meant to help Claude take a few products you found on CJ Dropshipping and turn them into one organized, branded product bundle for CCAC Pet Essentials.

You would upload screenshots of the CJ products you are considering, plus a screenshot of your current CCAC website categories. Claude then reviews what the products actually are, checks whether they make sense to sell together, decides which existing category they fit into, and suggests how to brand and present the bundle.

It is also designed to prevent Claude from guessing. If something like material, size, quantity, packaging, or supplier branding is not clear from the screenshots, the prompt tells Claude to flag it for verification instead of inventing information.

The prompt also helps with the practical Shopify side. It asks Claude to recommend the bundle name, product title, hook, benefits, how-to-use section, FAQs, SEO title, SEO description, product variants, and packaging approach.

So the main purpose is:

help you decide whether the products should really be bundled together
give the bundle a clear CCAC Pet Essentials identity
place it in the correct existing website category
create the product-page copy you can use in Shopify
organize colors, sizes, quantities, or other variants
identify whether the CJ products have supplier branding that may need to be changed
tell you what information still needs to be confirmed before you publish

For example, if you upload a pet toothbrush, dental wipes, and your CCAC category list, Claude should recognize that they may work as one oral-care bundle, determine which of your existing categories fits best, suggest several bundle names, and build the Shopify content around the combined offer.

In short, think of the prompt as a product bundle planning + branding + Shopify listing assistant. It takes raw CJ products and helps turn them into a more professional CCAC Pet Essentials product offer.

REQUIRED INPUTS:

uploaded screenshots of the CJ Dropshipping products you want to combine

Example:

an uploaded screenshot showing the current CCAC Pet Essentials website categories.
01.5

Product Bundle Logo & Packaging Design Prompt

Last edited in OneNote Friday, September 25, 2026

USE ChatGPT

This prompt is designed to take a brand concept that has already been selected—such as Fresh Grin—and turn it into a complete visual identity for a bundled pet product.

In simple terms, it tells ChatGPT to do four main things. First, it reviews the selected brand concept, tagline, product bundle, customer benefit, and the earlier Claude recommendations so the visual direction stays consistent with the original strategy. Second, it creates at least three different logo concepts, including the logo style, colors, fonts, icon ideas, and how the logo should appear on packaging, Shopify, and social media. Third, it creates at least three packaging concepts for the combined products, including the box, sleeve, pouch, insert card, front panel, back panel, and what information should appear on each side. Finally, it explains how the branding can start inexpensively and later grow into full private-label packaging.

The prompt is also meant to keep the branding realistic. It tells ChatGPT to study the actual CJ Dropshipping product screenshots, preserve the real product appearance, identify any existing supplier branding, and avoid pretending that a third-party branded product is already a CCAC private-label item. It separates what can be done now—such as branded inserts, sleeves, or Shopify imagery—from what would require custom packaging or manufacturer cooperation later.

For example, if the selected concept is Fresh Grin, the prompt would ask ChatGPT to develop three distinct visual directions for the brand rather than simply changing the colors of one logo. Each direction should include its own logo style, packaging approach, color palette, typography, brand personality, strengths, and limitations.

It also asks ChatGPT to create detailed prompts that you can later use with ChatGPT Image Generation to actually visualize the logo and packaging mockups. That means the output is not just branding advice—it can become the next step for generating real visual concepts.

REQUIRED INPUT:

The selected brand concept from a previous Claude analysis.
The Claude output describing the bundle, positioning, included products, target customer, tagline, category, packaging limitations, and branding recommendations/output results - refer to SECTION: 01: 01.4 New Product Branding Recommendations from Claude
Screenshots of the CJ Dropshipping products being combined.

Example:

If available, screenshots of the existing CCAC Pet Essentials website and category where the bundle will be sold.

The Genesis Workflow

02.1

INTRO: Understanding THE Genesis Workflow

Last edited in OneNote Monday, September 21, 2026

The Genesis workflow is a structured process that starts with analyzing your sales page, moves into deep customer and competitor research, and ends with identifying the beliefs customers need to develop before purchasing your product.

The goal is to have Claude produce research that you can use to improve your Shopify product page, develop your Meta advertising strategy, identify customer objections, and build advertising creatives around evidence-based selling points.

REMEMBER: Which Claude model should you use?

We are going to proceed with three (3) major phases, organized into seven (7) engineered prompts.

Sales page analysis - Evaluate your current product page and identify improvements.
Research methodology - Teach Claude how to conduct research using your supporting documents.
Deep product research - Investigate customers, competitors, objections, product differentiation, and market opportunities.
Customer avatar - Create a detailed profile of your prospective buyer.
Offer brief - Develop your product's positioning, selling points, benefits, and offer structure.
Marketing argument analysis - Understand how customer beliefs and logical selling arguments influence the structure of direct-response copy.
Necessary beliefs - Identify a maximum of six customer beliefs that your marketing needs to address.

The central idea in this Genesis Workflow is that effective marketing should be built around a compelling argument rather than relying only on exciting words. This emphasizes showing customers what makes a solution different and why that difference matters to them.

For example, for our pet hair remover, this means researching the customer's frustrations, understanding why existing cleaning methods may disappoint them, and investigating whether your product offers a demonstrable advantage.

The following prompts implement that approach while requiring Claude to distinguish verified facts from marketing hypotheses.
